newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says to raise May debenture coupon to 2.95 pct.
newsitem.headline: NCB says to raise May debenture coupon to 2.95 pct.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Tuesday it had set the coupon rate for its May five-year debenture to be sold on and after May 14 at 2.95 percent, up from 2.35 percent in April.
The bank also said it would raise its May long-term prime lending rate by 0.6 percentage point to 3.1 percent, effective from May 14.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month to reflect market trends.

The long-term credit banks customarily set their prime rate 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd's (IBJ) five-year debenture, which is the benchmark in Japan's debenture market. Bank debentures are the long-term credit banks' major fund-raising tool.
The IBJ announced on Monday that it would raise its long-term prime lending rate for May by 0.6 percentage point to 3.1 percent.

IBJ also said it would raise the coupon rate for its May five-year debenture to 2.2 percent from 1.6 percent in April. It was the first rise in the IBJ debenture coupon rate since it started on a downtrend last June.

Market yields on NCB debentures started to rise before those of the IBJ, due to fears over NCB's creditworthiness. But the spread between IBJ and NCB debentures has stabilised since an announcement in April that NCB and Bankers Trust New York Corp had agreed on a business alliance.
NCB last raised the coupon rate for its five-year debenture in February to 2.35 percent from 2.15 percent in January. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
